mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 4.0% signals a tightening monetary cycle that increases discount rates on equity cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0%, or the average 20-day return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.7% signals tightening labor market conditions that increase wage pressures and inflation expectations, prompting central bank hawkishness and reducing equity valuations over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE falls below 4.7%, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential investment (HOUST) above 1,000 thousand units signals strong household demand and confidence, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST exceeds 1000, or the average return in such periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a contraction in real output and labor market stress, triggering risk-off sentiment and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO declines and UNRATE rises, or the joint signal fails to produce a statistically significant negative average return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in CPIAUCSL above 210.0 with a 12-month increase exceeding 3.0% signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to maintain restrictive policy and suppress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 210.0 and 12-month growth exceeds 3.0%, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) above 380,000 million dollars, combined with rising industrial production (INDPRO), indicates strong aggregate demand and economic momentum, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS exceeds 380,000 and INDPRO rises, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in non-farm payroll growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs per month, combined with a declining unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a labor market overheating that increases inflationary pressure and prompts aggressive monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 and UNRATE is below 5.0%, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained expansion in real GDP (GDPC1) at a quarterly rate above 2.5% signals strong underlying economic growth, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.5% quarterly, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).
